key_insight: A large bilingual radiology dataset can train a single vision-language model to generate reports, answer questions, and localize findings without manual spatial annotations.
clinical_relevance: This approach could improve how medical AI supports radiology workflows by adding spatially verifiable outputs while preserving question-answering quality.
method: Built RefRad2D, a 1.2M CT/MR image-text dataset in German and English from clinical practice.
Used LLM-based curation plus automated segmentation to create VQA and spatial grounding subsets.
Trained RadGrounder for report generation, VQA, and grounding via bounding boxes or segmentation.
evidence_signal: On external benchmarks like Slake and VQA-RAD, the model was competitive with specialized medical VLMs, and adding the clinical data improved open-ended VQA without hurting language quality.
watch_item: The dataset and grounding labels are automatically generated, so real-world robustness and label noise should be carefully validated before deployment.
paper_title: Scalable Training of Spatially Grounded 2D Vision-Language Models for Radiology
